## File: README.md

# @mgpl-diagnostics/mail-kit

Mail for the MGPL Diagnostics backend. Mails are written in **our own mail design language**
(`.mail` sources, see [docs/language.md](docs/language.md)), never in hand-written HTML. mail-kit
checks them and compiles each one to email-safe HTML plus a plain-text part, in one consistent
design. It then sends them **through the worker's queue when one is available, or directly over
SMTP when it is not** (standalone).

- Zero runtime dependencies (its own SMTP client on `node:net`/`node:tls`, its own MIME builder).
- Every value is escaped; links, buttons and images accept safe URLs only.
- Syntax errors list every problem with `line:col`; missing data lists every missing variable.
- Built-in mails: password reset, password changed, staff invite, report ready, payment receipt.

## Install

```bash
# .npmrc: @mgpl-diagnostics:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
npm install @mgpl-diagnostics/mail-kit
```

## Use

```ts
import { createMailer, smtpTransport, queueAdapter, mailProcessor } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/mail-kit";

const mailer = createMailer({
  transport: smtpTransport(process.env.SMTP_URL!), // smtps://user:pass@smtp.example.com:465
  from: "Maa Gayatri Path Lab <no-reply@example.com>",
  brand: { name: "Maa Gayatri Path Lab", addressLines: ["Arang, Raipur, Chhattisgarh"] },
  // optional: the worker's BullMQ queue. Without it, or while Redis is down, mail goes out directly.
  queue: queueAdapter(mailQueue, { available: () => redis.status === "ready" }),
});

await mailer.send("password-reset", { name, email, link, expiresAt }, { to: { name, email } });
// → { via: "queue", jobId } or { via: "direct", messageId, accepted }

// in the worker process:
new Worker("mail", mailProcessor(mailer), { connection });
```

`send` renders first, so bad data or an unknown template fails in the request, not in the worker.
Jobs carry the template id, data and envelope (not HTML); finished jobs are removed at once
because a job can hold a single-use link.

### Your own mails

```ts
import { defineMail, MAIL_TEMPLATES } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/mail-kit";

const sampleReady = defineMail({
  id: "sample-collected",
  description: "Sample collected at home",
  source: `---
subject: We collected your sample
---
# Sample collected

Dear {{ patientName }}, your sample was collected at {{ at | time }}.
`,
  sample: { patientName: "Kavita Sharma", at: "2026-10-14T04:30:00Z" },
});

createMailer({ ..., templates: { ...MAIL_TEMPLATES, "sample-collected": sampleReady } });
```

### Transports

| Transport | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `smtpTransport(url \| options)` | Any SMTP server (Gmail, Zoho, Amazon SES, Brevo, Postfix). Implicit TLS on 465 or STARTTLS on 587; refuses to send in clear to a remote host. |
| `memoryTransport()` | Tests: `transport.sent` holds every message. |
| `fileTransport(dir)` | Local development: writes `.eml` files. |
| your own | Any `{ send(message) }`, e.g. a provider's HTTP API. |

## Commands

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build
npm run examples   # every built-in mail as .html / .txt / .eml in examples/ (git-ignored)
npm run llms       # regenerate llms-full.txt (CI fails when it is stale)
```

## File: AGENTS.md

# AGENTS.md — @mgpl-diagnostics/mail-kit

Mail for the MGPL Diagnostics backend: the **mail design language** (`.mail` sources), its compiler to
email-safe HTML + plain text, built-in mails, an SMTP transport, and a mailer that sends through the
worker's queue when available and directly otherwise. **A library: no server, no queue library, no
runtime dependencies.** The api repo wires it (container + worker).

## Map

```
src/types.ts       AST (Block, Inline, Expr), Theme, Brand, RenderedMail, OutgoingMessage, Transport
src/parse.ts       .mail parser: front matter, blocks, inline markup, {{ }} with filters; parseMail, checkMail
src/render.ts      renderMail → { subject, preheader, html, text }; escaping, safeUrl, filters (IST), mailVariables
src/theme.ts       DEFAULT_THEME ("Saffron & Neel" tokens), DEFAULT_BRAND, createTheme
src/define.ts      defineMail (parses at definition), MailTemplate
src/templates.ts   built-in mails + MAIL_TEMPLATES (fictional samples)
src/mime.ts        addresses, RFC 2047 headers, quoted-printable, buildMessage (multipart/alternative)
src/smtp.ts        smtpTransport (TLS 465 / STARTTLS 587, AUTH PLAIN/LOGIN), parseSmtpUrl
src/transports.ts  memoryTransport, fileTransport
src/mailer.ts      createMailer: send (queue → direct fallback), deliver (worker), MailJob, MailQueue
src/queue.ts       queueAdapter (BullMQ-shaped Queue), mailProcessor (BullMQ-shaped Worker)
docs/language.md   the language reference (keep it in step with parse.ts)
scripts/test.ts    language, safety, filters, built-ins, MIME, SMTP (in-process server), mailer
scripts/examples.ts  renders every built-in to examples/ (git-ignored)
```

## Rules

1. **No HTML in mail sources.** Mails are written in the language; the renderer owns all markup. Add a
   block or an inline style to the language (parser + both renderers + docs + tests) instead of an escape hatch.
2. **Everything printed is escaped**, and every URL goes through `safeUrl` (links: http(s)/mailto/tel;
   images: https). A test sends hostile data through every block; keep it passing.
3. **HTML and text say the same thing.** Every block renders in `Html` and `Text` in `render.ts`.
4. **Email-safe HTML only:** tables, inline styles, `bgcolor`; no scripts, external CSS, web fonts, SVG,
   flexbox or grid. Colours and sizes come from the theme, never hard-coded in a template.
5. **Errors are thorough:** syntax errors list every problem with line:col; missing data lists every
   path. Error codes (`MailError.code`) are a public contract: add, never rename.
6. **Queue jobs hold data, not HTML**, survive JSON (dates as ISO strings), and are removed on
   completion (they can hold reset links). `send` validates before enqueueing.
7. **Never send in clear to a remote SMTP host** (`requireTLS` defaults on except localhost).
   Never log message bodies or SMTP credentials.
8. Zero runtime dependencies. Queue and worker types are structural (no bullmq import).
9. Samples use fictional people and `example.com` addresses. The lab's real contact details live only in
   report-kit's `lab.ts`; the api passes them in as the brand.
10. Dates print in IST; money is integer paise (`money` filter).

## Commands

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build
npm run examples   # look at the HTML after changing the renderer or theme
npm run llms       # regenerate llms-full.txt (CI fails when it is stale)
```

## Licence

All rights reserved (see LICENSE).

## File: docs/language.md

# The MGPL mail design language

Mails are written in `.mail` sources, not HTML. mail-kit checks them, then compiles each one to
**email-safe HTML** (tables and inline styles, which every mail app understands) and a **plain-text
part**. The design (colours, spacing, header, footer, buttons) comes from the theme, so every mail
looks the same and nobody hand-writes HTML. The source cannot contain HTML: `<b>` prints as text.

```text
---
subject: Reset your password
preheader: This link works until {{ expiresAt | time }}.
---
# Reset your password

Hi {{ name }}, we received a request to reset the password of your MGPL account.

::button href="{{ link }}"
Choose a new password
::

::callout tone="warning" title="Didn't ask for this?"
Ignore this mail. Your password stays the same.
::
```

## Front matter

Between two `---` lines at the top. `subject` is required.

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `subject` | Subject line. Variables allowed. |
| `preheader` | Preview text shown next to the subject in the inbox. Default: the first paragraph. |
| `footer` | A note printed above the brand footer (e.g. "Please do not forward this report"). |

## Text

| Write | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `# Title`, `## Section`, `### Small` | Headings (brand colour) |
| Lines separated by a blank line | Paragraphs. A line ending in `\` keeps a line break. |
| `- item` or `* item`; `1. item` | Lists. Indented lines continue the item. |
| `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` `` | Inline styles |
| `[label](https://…)` | Link (http, https, mailto or tel only) |
| `{{ name }}`, `{{ patient.name }}` | A value from the data, always escaped |
| `\*`, `\[`, `\|` | The character itself |
| `// note` | A comment line (not printed) |

## Blocks

A block starts with `::name attr="value"` and ends with a line holding only `::`. Blocks marked
"single line" have no body and no closing `::`.

| Block | Attributes | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `::button` | `href` (required), `tone="primary"\|"secondary"` | One line: the label |
| `::callout` | `tone="info"\|"success"\|"warning"\|"danger"`, `title` | Any blocks |
| `::card` | — | Any blocks, on a tinted panel |
| `::rows` | — | `Label \| value` per line: a summary list |
| `::table` | `align="l r c…"` (one per column), `footer` (last line is a total row) | First line is the header; cells split by `\|` |
| `::code` | — | Lines shown large and monospaced (OTPs, codes) |
| `::divider` | — | single line |
| `::spacer` | `size` (4–96 px, default 24) | single line |
| `::image` | `src` (https), `alt` (required), `width` (16–600) | single line |

### Repeating rows

In `::table` and `::rows`, a line starting with `@each list as item:` is repeated for each item:

```text
::table align="l r" footer
Item | Amount
@each items as item: {{ item.name }} | {{ item.amount | money }}
Total | {{ total | money }}
::
```

## Conditions and loops

```text
::if due
::callout tone="warning" title="Balance due: {{ due | money }}"
Reports are released after full payment.
::
::else
Paid in full.
::

::if !items
Nothing to show.
::

::each roles as role
- **{{ role.name }}** ({{ loop.index }} of many)
::
```

`::if` is true for a non-empty value or list, `!` negates. Inside `::each`, `loop.index` (from 1),
`loop.first` and `loop.last` are available. Lists produced by `::each` join into one list.

## Filters

`{{ value | filter }}`, chained left to right.

| Filter | Input | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `money` | integer paise | `₹1,23,456.50` (Indian grouping) |
| `number` | number | `12,34,567` |
| `date` | Date, ISO string or IST day `"2026-10-14"` | `14 Oct 2026` |
| `time` | Date or ISO string | `9:30 pm IST` |
| `datetime` | Date or ISO string | `14 Oct 2026, 9:30 pm IST` |
| `upper`, `lower` | text | case changed |
| `default: "text"` | anything | used when the value is missing or empty |

All dates are shown in IST. Queued mails cross JSON, so Dates arrive as ISO strings; the filters
accept both.

## Errors

- **Syntax** (`MailSyntaxError`, code `MAIL_SYNTAX`): every problem in the source with
  `file:line:col`. `defineMail` parses at startup, so a broken template fails the build and tests,
  never a send. `checkMail(source)` returns the same list without throwing (editors, CI).
- **Missing data** (`MissingVariableError`, `MAIL_MISSING_VARIABLE`): all missing paths at once.
  Values inside a false `::if` are not needed.
- **Unsafe URL** (`MAIL_UNSAFE_URL`): links and buttons take http(s), mailto and tel; images take https.
- **Bad value** (`MAIL_BAD_VALUE`): e.g. `money` on a non-integer, or printing an object.

## Design tokens

`DEFAULT_THEME` is "Saffron & Neel" (the website palette): navy header and headings, saffron
buttons and accent rule, sandstone canvas. `createTheme({ colors: { accent: "#…" } })` changes
tokens. The brand (name, logo URL, address lines, phone, email, website) is passed by the caller;
the api passes the lab profile from report-kit, the only place the lab's contact details live.

## File: llms.txt

# @mgpl-diagnostics/mail-kit

> Mail for the MGPL Diagnostics backend (Node.js ≥ 20, zero runtime dependencies). Mails are written in the MGPL mail design language (`.mail`: front matter, Markdown-like text, `::button`/`::callout`/`::card`/`::rows`/`::table`/`::code`/`::divider`/`::spacer`/`::image` blocks, `::if`/`::each`, `{{ var | filter }}`), compiled to email-safe HTML plus plain text in one theme, and sent through the worker's queue when available or directly over SMTP.

Key facts for agents:
- `createMailer({ transport, from, queue?, brand?, theme?, templates? })`; `mailer.send(id, data, { to })` → `{ via: "queue", jobId }` or `{ via: "direct", messageId, accepted }`; the worker runs `mailProcessor(mailer)`.
- `queueAdapter(bullmqQueue, { available: () => redis.status === "ready" })`; failures fall back to direct sending (or throw with `whenQueueFails: "throw"`).
- `smtpTransport("smtps://user:pass@host:465")`, `memoryTransport()`, `fileTransport(dir)`.
- `defineMail({ id, description, source, sample })`; `parseMail`, `checkMail`, `renderMail`, `mailVariables`.
- Filters: money (integer paise), number, date, time, datetime (IST), upper, lower, default.
- Errors: `MailError.code` = MAIL_SYNTAX, MAIL_MISSING_VARIABLE, MAIL_BAD_VALUE, MAIL_UNSAFE_URL, MAIL_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE, MAIL_BAD_ADDRESS, MAIL_TRANSPORT, MAIL_QUEUE.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): usage, transports, custom mails
- [docs/language.md](docs/language.md): the mail design language
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): map and rules

## Source

- [src/parse.ts](src/parse.ts): parser
- [src/render.ts](src/render.ts): HTML + text renderer
- [src/mailer.ts](src/mailer.ts): queue / direct mailer
- [src/smtp.ts](src/smtp.ts): SMTP client
- [src/templates.ts](src/templates.ts): built-in mails

## File: scripts/examples.ts

```ts
// Renders every built-in mail with its sample data into examples/ (git-ignored): <id>.html,
// <id>.txt and <id>.eml. Open the .html in a browser or the .eml in a mail app.
import { mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { buildMessage, MAIL_TEMPLATES } from "../src/index";

const brand = {
  name: "Maa Gayatri Path Lab",
  addressLines: ["Arang, Raipur, Chhattisgarh"],
  phone: "+91-00000-00000",
  website: "https://example.com",
};
mkdirSync("examples", { recursive: true });
for (const t of Object.values(MAIL_TEMPLATES)) {
  const r = t.render(t.sample as never, { brand });
  writeFileSync(`examples/${t.id}.html`, r.html);
  writeFileSync(`examples/${t.id}.txt`, r.text);
  const eml = buildMessage({ from: "MGPL <no-reply@example.com>", to: "Kavita Sharma <kavita.sharma@example.com>", subject: r.subject, html: r.html, text: r.text });
  writeFileSync(`examples/${t.id}.eml`, eml.raw);
  console.log(`examples/${t.id}.html  ${r.subject}`);
}
```

## File: scripts/llms-full.mjs

````js
// Builds llms-full.txt: every doc and source file of the repo in one plain-text document for AI tools.
//   node scripts/llms-full.mjs "<title>" <file-or-folder> [file-or-folder …]
// Folders are walked recursively. Output order: README, AGENTS, docs, then the rest alphabetically.
// Skipped: build output, dependencies, lockfiles, generated files, binaries. Files over 150 KB are
// listed (path + size) instead of inlined. CI checks the file is up to date (`npm run llms` + git diff).
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { extname, join, relative } from "node:path";

const [title, ...inputs] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!title || !inputs.length) {
  console.error('usage: node scripts/llms-full.mjs "<title>" <file-or-folder> …');
  process.exit(1);
}

const TEXT = new Set([".ts", ".tsx", ".mts", ".cts", ".js", ".mjs", ".cjs", ".md", ".mdx", ".json", ".css", ".yml", ".yaml", ".txt", ".graphql", ".gql", ".sql", ".html"]);
const SKIP_DIRS = new Set(["node_modules", "dist", ".next", ".git", ".turbo", "coverage", "examples", ".pg-test"]);
const SKIP_FILES = /(^|\/)(package-lock\.json|pnpm-lock\.yaml|yarn\.lock|llms-full\.txt|[^/]*\.generated\.[^/]+|[^/]*\.log)$/;
const MAX = 150 * 1024;
const LANG = { ".ts": "ts", ".tsx": "tsx", ".mts": "ts", ".cts": "ts", ".js": "js", ".mjs": "js", ".cjs": "js", ".json": "json", ".css": "css", ".yml": "yaml", ".yaml": "yaml", ".graphql": "graphql", ".gql": "graphql", ".sql": "sql", ".html": "html" };

const posix = (p) => p.split("\\").join("/");
const files = new Set();
function walk(p) {
  const st = statSync(p);
  if (st.isDirectory()) {
    for (const name of readdirSync(p)) if (!SKIP_DIRS.has(name)) walk(join(p, name));
  } else if (TEXT.has(extname(p).toLowerCase()) && !SKIP_FILES.test(posix(p))) {
    files.add(posix(relative(".", p)));
  }
}
for (const input of inputs) walk(input);

const rank = (f) => (/^README\.md$/i.test(f) ? 0 : /^AGENTS\.md$/i.test(f) ? 1 : /^docs\//.test(f) ? 2 : 3);
const ordered = [...files].sort((a, b) => rank(a) - rank(b) || (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0));

const parts = [`# ${title} — full documentation and source\n\n> Generated by scripts/llms-full.mjs. Do not edit by hand. ${ordered.length} files.\n\n## Contents\n\n${ordered.map((f) => `- ${f}`).join("\n")}\n`];
const omitted = [];
for (const f of ordered) {
  // LF-normalised text, so Windows and Linux checkouts produce byte-identical output
  const body = readFileSync(f, "utf8").replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").trim();
  const size = Buffer.byteLength(body);
  if (size > MAX) {
    omitted.push(`${f} (${(size / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB)`);
    parts.push(`\n\n---\n\n## File: ${f}\n\n_Omitted: ${(size / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB. Read the file directly._\n`);
    continue;
  }
  const lang = LANG[extname(f).toLowerCase()];
  const fence = body.includes("```") ? "````" : "```";
  parts.push(`\n\n---\n\n## File: ${f}\n\n${lang ? `${fence}${lang}\n${body}\n${fence}` : body}\n`);
}
const out = parts.join("");
writeFileSync("llms-full.txt", out);
console.log(`llms-full.txt: ${ordered.length} files, ${(out.length / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB${omitted.length ? `; omitted (too large): ${omitted.join(", ")}` : ""}`);
````

## File: scripts/test.ts

```ts
// mail-kit checks: language (parse errors with positions, inline markup, blocks, control flow),
// rendering safety (escaping, URLs), filters, every built-in mail, MIME, SMTP against an
// in-process server, and the mailer's queue / direct fallback.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { createServer, type Socket } from "node:net";
import {
  buildMessage,
  checkMail,
  createMailer,
  createTheme,
  defineMail,
  encodeWord,
  MAIL_TEMPLATES,
  mailProcessor,
  MailError,
  MailSyntaxError,
  memoryTransport,
  MissingVariableError,
  parseAddress,
  parseMail,
  parseSmtpUrl,
  quotedPrintable,
  queueAdapter,
  renderMail,
  smtpTransport,
  TransportError,
  type MailJob,
} from "../src/index";

let passed = 0;
const failures: string[] = [];
async function check(name: string, fn: () => unknown): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await fn();
    passed++;
  } catch (e) {
    failures.push(`✗ ${name}\n    ${(e as Error).stack?.split("\n").slice(0, 3).join("\n    ")}`);
  }
}

const mail = (body: string, front = "subject: Hi") => `---\n${front}\n---\n${body}`;
const render = (src: string, data: Record<string, unknown> = {}) => renderMail(parseMail(src), data);
const syntaxErrors = (src: string) => {
  try {
    parseMail(src);
  } catch (e) {
    assert.ok(e instanceof MailSyntaxError, String(e));
    return e.diagnostics;
  }
  assert.fail("expected a syntax error");
};

// ---- language ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

await check("headings, paragraphs, lists and hard breaks", () => {
  const doc = parseMail(mail("# Title\n\nline one\nline two\\\nafter break\n\n- a\n- b\n\n1. x\n2. y\n\n## Sub\n### Small"));
  assert.deepEqual(doc.body.map((b) => b.kind), ["heading", "paragraph", "list", "list", "heading", "heading"]);
  const p = doc.body[1]!;
  assert.ok(p.kind === "paragraph" && p.content.some((n) => n.kind === "br"));
  const l = doc.body[3]!;
  assert.ok(l.kind === "list" && l.ordered && l.items.length === 2);
});

await check("inline markup: strong, em, code, link, variables, escapes", () => {
  const r = render(mail("**bold** *em* _em2_ `x<y` [site](https://a.example/{{ id }}) {{ name }} \\*not em\\* snake_case_word"), { id: 7, name: "A" });
  assert.match(r.html, /<strong[^>]*>bold<\/strong>/);
  assert.match(r.html, /<em[^>]*>em<\/em>/);
  assert.match(r.html, /<em[^>]*>em2<\/em>/);
  assert.match(r.html, /<code[^>]*>x&lt;y<\/code>/);
  assert.match(r.html, /<a href="https:\/\/a\.example\/7"[^>]*>site<\/a>/);
  assert.match(r.html, /\*not em\*/);
  assert.match(r.html, /snake_case_word/);
  assert.match(r.text, /site \(https:\/\/a\.example\/7\)/);
});

await check("front matter: subject required, unknown keys refused", () => {
  assert.match(syntaxErrors("# no front matter")[0]!.message, /subject/);
  const d = syntaxErrors("---\nsubject: x\ncolour: red\n---\nhi");
  assert.equal(d[0]!.line, 3);
  assert.match(syntaxErrors("---\nsubject: x\nhello")[0]!.message, /not closed/);
});

await check("errors carry line and column, and all are reported at once", () => {
  const d = syntaxErrors(mail("ok\n\n::buton href=x\nGo\n::\n\n{{ name | shout }}\n\n::callout tone=loud\nx\n::"));
  assert.equal(d.length, 3, JSON.stringify(d));
  assert.deepEqual([d[0]!.line, d[0]!.col], [6, 1]);
  assert.match(d[0]!.message, /Unknown block "::buton"/);
  assert.match(d[1]!.message, /Unknown filter "shout"/);
  assert.equal(d[1]!.line, 10);
  assert.match(d[2]!.message, /tone must be/);
  // error messages name the file
  try {
    parseMail(mail("::nope"), "welcome.mail");
  } catch (e) {
    assert.match((e as Error).message, /^welcome\.mail:4:1 /);
  }
});

await check("block rules: required and unknown attributes, unclosed blocks, stray closers", () => {
  assert.match(syntaxErrors(mail("::button\nGo\n::"))[0]!.message, /needs href/);
  assert.match(syntaxErrors(mail("::button href=x size=2\nGo\n::"))[0]!.message, /no attribute "size"/);
  assert.match(syntaxErrors(mail("::card\ntext"))[0]!.message, /"::card" is not closed/);
  assert.match(syntaxErrors(mail("text\n::"))[0]!.message, /closes nothing/);
  assert.match(syntaxErrors(mail("::else"))[0]!.message, /only allowed inside/);
  assert.match(syntaxErrors(mail("::button href=x\nOne\nTwo\n::"))[0]!.message, /exactly one line/);
  assert.match(syntaxErrors(mail("::table\nA | B\n1 | 2 | 3\n::"))[0]!.message, /3 cells; the header has 2/);
  assert.match(syntaxErrors(mail("::table align=\"l\"\nA | B\n1 | 2\n::"))[0]!.message, /align/);
  assert.match(syntaxErrors(mail("::spacer size=999"))[0]!.message, /4 to 96/);
  assert.match(syntaxErrors(mail("::each items\nx\n::"))[0]!.message, /items as item/);
  assert.match(syntaxErrors(mail("::rows\n@each x y: a | b\n::"))[0]!.message, /@each items as item/);
});

await check("checkMail returns diagnostics without throwing", () => {
  assert.deepEqual(checkMail(mail("fine")), []);
  assert.equal(checkMail(mail("::nope")).length, 1);
});

await check("::if / ::else / negation and ::each with loop variables", () => {
  const src = mail("::if vip\nVIP\n::else\nRegular\n::\n\n::if !items\nNone\n::\n\n::each items as it\n{{ loop.index }}. {{ it.name }}{{ loop.last | default: \"\" }}\n::");
  const a = render(src, { vip: true, items: [{ name: "A" }, { name: "B" }] });
  assert.match(a.text, /VIP/);
  assert.doesNotMatch(a.text, /Regular|None/);
  assert.match(a.text, /1\. A/);
  assert.match(a.text, /2\. B/);
  const b = render(src, { vip: false, items: [] });
  assert.match(b.text, /Regular/);
  assert.match(b.text, /None/);
});

await check("lists built by ::each are one list", () => {
  const r = render(mail("::each xs as x\n- {{ x }}\n::"), { xs: ["a", "b", "c"] });
  assert.equal((r.html.match(/<ul /g) ?? []).length, 1);
  assert.equal((r.html.match(/<li /g) ?? []).length, 3);
  assert.match(r.text, /- a\n- b\n- c/);
});

await check("tables and rows: alignment, @each rows, footer, pipes inside variables", () => {
  const src = mail("::table align=\"l r\" footer\nItem | Amount\n@each items as i: {{ i.name }} | {{ i.p | money }}\nTotal | {{ total | money | default: \"0\" }}\n::\n\n::rows\nA \\| B | {{ x }}\n@each extra as e: {{ e.k }} | {{ e.v }}\n::");
  const r = render(src, { items: [{ name: "CBC", p: 39900 }, { name: "TSH", p: 29900 }], total: 69800, x: "1", extra: [{ k: "K", v: "V" }] });
  assert.match(r.html, /<th align="right"[^>]*>Amount<\/th>/);
  assert.match(r.html, /₹698\.00/);
  assert.match(r.text, /CBC\s+₹399\.00\nTSH\s+₹299\.00\n-+\s+-+\nTotal\s+₹698\.00/);
  assert.match(r.text, /A \| B: 1/);
  assert.match(r.text, /K:\s+V/);
});

await check("code, divider, spacer, image, card, callout", () => {
  const r = render(mail("::code\n{{ otp }}\n::\n\n::divider\n::spacer size=12\n::image src=\"https://cdn.example/x.png\" alt=\"Logo\" width=120\n\n::card\nIn a card\n::\n\n::callout tone=success title=\"Done {{ n }}\"\nok\n::"), { otp: "482913", n: 2 });
  assert.match(r.html, /482913/);
  assert.match(r.html, /<img src="https:\/\/cdn\.example\/x\.png" alt="Logo" width="120"/);
  assert.match(r.html, /Done 2/);
  assert.match(r.text, /^ {4}482913$/m);
  assert.match(r.text, /\| Done 2\n\|\n\| ok/);
  assert.match(r.text, /\[Logo\]/);
});

// ---- safety ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

await check("every value is escaped (no HTML injection through data)", () => {
  const evil = `<script>alert(1)</script>"'&`;
  const r = render(mail("# {{ x }}\n\n{{ x }}\n\n::rows\n{{ x }} | {{ x }}\n::\n\n::callout title=\"{{ x }}\"\n{{ x }}\n::", "subject: {{ x }}"), { x: evil });
  assert.ok(!r.html.includes("<script>"));
  assert.ok(r.html.includes("&lt;script&gt;alert(1)&lt;/script&gt;&quot;&#39;&amp;"));
  assert.equal(r.subject, evil);
  // source text is escaped too: the language has no raw HTML
  assert.ok(!render(mail("<b>hi</b>")).html.includes("<b>hi</b>"));
});

await check("unsafe URLs are refused in links, buttons and images", () => {
  for (const href of ["javascript:alert(1)", "JaVaScRiPt:alert(1)", "data:text/html,x", "//evil.example", "/relative", "https://a b"]) {
    assert.throws(() => render(mail("::button href=\"{{ u }}\"\nGo\n::"), { u: href }), (e: unknown) => e instanceof MailError && e.code === "MAIL_UNSAFE_URL", href);
    assert.throws(() => render(mail("[x]({{ u }})"), { u: href }), MailError, href);
  }
  assert.throws(() => render(mail("::image src=\"http://a.example/x.png\" alt=x")), /https/);
  for (const ok of ["https://a.example/?q=1&b=2", "http://localhost:3000/reset", "mailto:a@b.in", "tel:+91-9000000000"]) {
    const r = render(mail("::button href=\"{{ u }}\"\nGo\n::"), { u: ok });
    assert.ok(r.html.includes(`href="${ok.replace(/&/g, "&amp;")}"`), ok);
  }
});

await check("missing variables are all reported at once; defaults and empty strings are fine", () => {
  const src = mail("{{ a }} {{ b.c }} {{ d | default: \"-\" }} {{ e }}", "subject: {{ s }}");
  try {
    render(src, { e: "" });
    assert.fail("expected MissingVariableError");
  } catch (e) {
    assert.ok(e instanceof MissingVariableError);
    assert.deepEqual(e.paths.sort(), ["a", "b.c", "s"]);
    assert.equal(e.code, "MAIL_MISSING_VARIABLE");
  }
  assert.throws(() => render(mail("::each xs as x\n{{ x }}\n::")), MissingVariableError);
  assert.throws(() => render(mail("{{ o }}"), { o: { a: 1 } }), /cannot be printed/);
});

// ---- filters -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

await check("filters: money (paise, Indian grouping), number, dates in IST, case, default", () => {
  const r = render(
    mail("{{ m | money }}|{{ big | money }}|{{ n | number }}|{{ d | date }}|{{ d | time }}|{{ d | datetime }}|{{ day | date }}|{{ s | upper }}|{{ s | lower }}|{{ dd | datetime }}"),
    { m: 39950, big: 12345678900, n: 1234567, d: "2026-10-14T18:45:00Z", day: "2026-10-14", s: "MiXeD", dd: new Date("2026-03-31T18:30:00Z") },
  );
  const first = r.text.split("\n\n")[0]!;
  assert.equal(first.replace(/\s+/g, " "), "₹399.50|₹12,34,56,789.00|12,34,567|15 Oct 2026|12:15 am IST|15 Oct 2026, 12:15 am IST|14 Oct 2026|MIXED|mixed|1 Apr 2026, 12:00 am IST");
  assert.throws(() => render(mail("{{ m | money }}"), { m: 10.5 }), /integer paise/);
  assert.throws(() => render(mail("{{ d | time }}"), { d: "2026-10-14" }), /needs a time/);
  assert.throws(() => render(mail("{{ d | date }}"), { d: "not a date" }), /Date or an ISO/);
});

// ---- layout and theme --------------------------------------------------------------------------

await check("layout: brand header and footer, preheader, theme tokens, mobile CSS", () => {
  const brand = { name: "Test Lab", logoUrl: "https://cdn.example/logo.png", addressLines: ["Line 1"], phone: "+91-1", email: "lab@example.com", website: "https://lab.example" };
  const theme = createTheme({ colors: { accent: "#0B7285" } });
  const r = renderMail(parseMail(mail("Body text here.\n\n::button href=\"https://x.example\"\nGo\n::", "subject: S\nfooter: Note {{ n }}")), { n: 1 }, { brand, theme });
  assert.match(r.html, /<img src="https:\/\/cdn\.example\/logo\.png" alt="Test Lab"/);
  assert.match(r.html, /Line 1<br>\+91-1  \|  lab@example\.com  \|  https:\/\/lab\.example/);
  assert.match(r.html, /background-color:#0B7285/);
  assert.match(r.html, /@media \(max-width:620px\)/);
  assert.equal(r.preheader, "Body text here.");
  assert.match(r.html, /display:none[^>]*>Body text here\./);
  assert.match(r.text, /--\nNote 1\n\nTest Lab\nLine 1\n/);
  assert.ok(r.html.startsWith("<!DOCTYPE html>"));
  assert.ok(!/<script|<link|<style[^>]*@import/i.test(r.html), "no scripts or external CSS");
});

await check("plain text wraps at 76 columns (URLs stay whole)", () => {
  const long = "word ".repeat(60).trim();
  const r = render(mail(`${long}\n\n[x](https://example.com/${"a".repeat(100)})`));
  for (const line of r.text.split("\n")) if (!line.includes("https://")) assert.ok(line.length <= 76, line);
  assert.ok(r.text.includes(`https://example.com/${"a".repeat(100)}`));
});

// ---- built-in mails ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

for (const t of Object.values(MAIL_TEMPLATES)) {
  await check(`built-in "${t.id}" renders its sample and its sample covers every variable`, () => {
    const r = t.render(t.sample as never);
    assert.ok(r.subject && r.html.length > 1000 && r.text.length > 50);
    const body = r.html.slice(r.html.indexOf("<body"));
    assert.ok(!/\{\{|\}\}|::/.test(r.text + body), "no unrendered markup");
    const sample = t.sample as Record<string, unknown>;
    for (const v of t.variables) {
      const [head] = v.split(".");
      assert.ok(head! in sample, `sample lacks ${v}`);
    }
    // each mail fails loudly without its data
    assert.throws(() => t.render({} as never), MissingVariableError);
    // no real contact details in the package
    assert.ok(!/@gmail\.com|\+91-9\d{9}/.test(t.source));
  });
}

await check("defineMail fails at definition on a syntax error", () => {
  assert.throws(() => defineMail({ id: "bad", description: "", source: mail("::nope"), sample: {} }), /bad:4:1/);
});

// ---- MIME --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

await check("addresses: forms, validation, no header injection", () => {
  assert.deepEqual(parseAddress("Kavita Sharma <kavita@example.com>"), { name: "Kavita Sharma", email: "kavita@example.com" });
  assert.deepEqual(parseAddress({ email: "a@b.in" }), { email: "a@b.in" });
  for (const bad of ["no-at", "a@b", "a@b.in\r\nBcc: x@y.in", "<a@b.in>\nX: y", "a b@c.in"]) {
    assert.throws(() => parseAddress(bad), (e: unknown) => e instanceof MailError && e.code === "MAIL_BAD_ADDRESS", bad);
  }
  assert.throws(() => buildMessage({ from: "a@b.in", to: "c@d.in", subject: "x\r\nBcc: e@f.in", html: "", text: "" }), /line breaks/);
  assert.throws(() => buildMessage({ from: "a@b.in", to: "c@d.in", subject: "x", html: "", text: "", headers: { "X-A": "1\nB: 2" } }), /line breaks/);
  assert.throws(() => buildMessage({ from: "a@b.in", to: "c@d.in", subject: "x", html: "", text: "", headers: { Bcc: "e@f.in" } }), /set by mail-kit/);
});

await check("quoted-printable: line length, '=' and UTF-8, trailing space", () => {
  const qp = quotedPrintable(`${"x".repeat(200)}\n₹ 1 = 1 \nend`);
  for (const l of qp.split("\r\n")) assert.ok(l.length <= 76, l);
  assert.ok(qp.includes("=E2=82=B9"));
  assert.ok(qp.includes("=3D"));
  assert.ok(qp.includes("1=20\r\nend"));
  const decoded = Buffer.from(qp.replace(/=\r\n/g, "").replace(/=([0-9A-F]{2})/g, (_, h: string) => String.fromCharCode(parseInt(h, 16))), "latin1").toString("utf8");
  assert.equal(decoded, `${"x".repeat(200)}\r\n₹ 1 = 1 \r\nend`);
});

await check("encoded headers: UTF-8 subjects and names, each word under 76", () => {
  const w = encodeWord("रिपोर्ट तैयार है — आपकी जाँच के नतीजे देखें ₹399");
  for (const part of w.split("\r\n ")) assert.ok(part.length <= 75 && /^=\?UTF-8\?B\?.+\?=$/.test(part), part);
  const decoded = w.split("\r\n ").map((p) => Buffer.from(p.slice(10, -2), "base64").toString("utf8")).join("");
  assert.equal(decoded, "रिपोर्ट तैयार है — आपकी जाँच के नतीजे देखें ₹399");
  const m = buildMessage({ from: { name: "लैब", email: "a@b.in" }, to: "c@d.in", bcc: ["e@f.in", "c@d.in"], subject: "Hi", html: "<p>x</p>", text: "x" });
  assert.match(m.raw, /^From: =\?UTF-8\?B\?/);
  assert.ok(!/^Bcc:/im.test(m.raw), "Bcc never appears in headers");
  assert.deepEqual(m.recipients, ["c@d.in", "e@f.in"]);
  assert.match(m.raw, /Content-Type: multipart\/alternative; boundary="mk_[0-9a-f]+"/);
  assert.match(m.messageId, /^<[^@]+@b\.in>$/);
});

// ---- SMTP --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

interface FakeOpts {
  auth?: "PLAIN" | "LOGIN";
  rejectRcpt?: string;
  startTls?: boolean;
}
interface Received {
  from: string;
  rcpt: string[];
  data: string;
  auth: string[];
}
async function fakeSmtp(o: FakeOpts = {}) {
  const received: Received[] = [];
  const server = createServer((sock: Socket) => {
    const cur: Received = { from: "", rcpt: [], data: "", auth: [] };
    let mode: "cmd" | "data" | "login-user" | "login-pass" = "cmd";
    let buf = "";
    const say = (s: string) => sock.write(s + "\r\n");
    say("220 fake ESMTP");
    sock.on("data", (d) => {
      buf += d.toString("latin1");
      let nl: number;
      while ((nl = buf.indexOf("\r\n")) >= 0) {
        const line = buf.slice(0, nl);
        buf = buf.slice(nl + 2);
        if (mode === "data") {
          if (line === ".") {
            mode = "cmd";
            received.push({ ...cur, rcpt: [...cur.rcpt] });
            say("250 2.0.0 queued");
          } else cur.data += line + "\r\n";
          continue;
        }
        if (mode === "login-user") {
          cur.auth.push(Buffer.from(line, "base64").toString());
          mode = "login-pass";
          say("334 UGFzc3dvcmQ6");
          continue;
        }
        if (mode === "login-pass") {
          cur.auth.push(Buffer.from(line, "base64").toString());
          mode = "cmd";
          say(cur.auth[1] === "secret" ? "235 ok" : "535 bad credentials");
          continue;
        }
        const [verb] = line.split(" ");
        switch (verb!.toUpperCase()) {
          case "EHLO":
            sock.write(`250-fake\r\n${o.startTls ? "250-STARTTLS\r\n" : ""}${o.auth ? `250-AUTH ${o.auth}\r\n` : ""}250 8BITMIME\r\n`);
            break;
          case "AUTH": {
            const [, mech, arg] = line.split(" ");
            if (mech === "LOGIN") {
              mode = "login-user";
              say("334 VXNlcm5hbWU6");
            } else {
              const [, u, p] = Buffer.from(arg!, "base64").toString().split("\0");
              cur.auth.push(u!, p!);
              say(p === "secret" ? "235 ok" : "535 bad credentials");
            }
            break;
          }
          case "MAIL":
            cur.from = /<(.*)>/.exec(line)![1]!;
            say("250 ok");
            break;
          case "RCPT": {
            const r = /<(.*)>/.exec(line)![1]!;
            if (r === o.rejectRcpt) say("550 no such user");
            else {
              cur.rcpt.push(r);
              say("250 ok");
            }
            break;
          }
          case "DATA":
            mode = "data";
            say("354 go ahead");
            break;
          case "QUIT":
            say("221 bye");
            sock.end();
            break;
          default:
            say("502 not implemented");
        }
      }
    });
  });
  await new Promise<void>((r) => server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", r));
  const port = (server.address() as { port: number }).port;
  return { port, received, close: () => new Promise<void>((r) => server.close(() => r())) };
}

const msg = (extra: Partial<Parameters<typeof buildMessage>[0]> = {}) => ({
  from: "MGPL <no-reply@example.com>",
  to: "Kavita Sharma <kavita@example.com>",
  subject: "Résumé of your tests",
  html: "<p>Hello</p>",
  text: "Hello\n.leading dot line\n..two dots",
  ...extra,
});

await check("SMTP: AUTH PLAIN, envelope, dot-stuffing, message arrives intact", async () => {
  const s = await fakeSmtp({ auth: "PLAIN" });
  try {
    const t = smtpTransport({ host: "127.0.0.1", port: s.port, user: "lab", pass: "secret" });
    const res = await t.send(msg({ cc: "cc@example.com", bcc: "hidden@example.com" }));
    assert.deepEqual(res.accepted, ["kavita@example.com", "cc@example.com", "hidden@example.com"]);
    const got = s.received[0]!;
    assert.equal(got.from, "no-reply@example.com");
    assert.deepEqual(got.auth, ["lab", "secret"]);
    assert.ok(got.data.includes("\r\n..leading dot line\r\n...two dots"), "dot-stuffed");
    const unstuffed = got.data.replace(/^\.\./gm, ".");
    assert.ok(unstuffed.includes(".leading dot line\r\n..two dots"));
    assert.ok(!/^Bcc:/im.test(got.data));
    assert.match(got.data, /^Subject: =\?UTF-8\?B\?/m);
    assert.ok(got.data.includes(`Message-ID: ${res.messageId}`));
  } finally {
    await s.close();
  }
});

await check("SMTP: AUTH LOGIN, wrong password is a TransportError with status, password not in message", async () => {
  const s = await fakeSmtp({ auth: "LOGIN" });
  try {
    await smtpTransport({ host: "127.0.0.1", port: s.port, user: "lab", pass: "secret" }).send(msg());
    assert.equal(s.received.length, 1);
    await assert.rejects(
      smtpTransport({ host: "127.0.0.1", port: s.port, user: "lab", pass: "wrong" }).send(msg()),
      (e: unknown) => e instanceof TransportError && e.status === 535 && !e.message.includes("wrong") && e.message.includes("(credentials)"),
    );
  } finally {
    await s.close();
  }
});

await check("SMTP: a refused recipient is skipped; all refused fails", async () => {
  const s = await fakeSmtp({ rejectRcpt: "nobody@example.com" });
  try {
    const t = smtpTransport({ host: "127.0.0.1", port: s.port });
    const r = await t.send(msg({ to: ["kavita@example.com", "nobody@example.com"] }));
    assert.deepEqual(r.accepted, ["kavita@example.com"]);
    await assert.rejects(t.send(msg({ to: "nobody@example.com" })), (e: unknown) => e instanceof TransportError && e.status === 550);
  } finally {
    await s.close();
  }
});

await check("SMTP: refuses to send in clear when TLS is required", async () => {
  const s = await fakeSmtp({ auth: "PLAIN" });
  try {
    await assert.rejects(smtpTransport({ host: "127.0.0.1", port: s.port, requireTLS: true, user: "u", pass: "secret" }).send(msg()), /does not offer TLS/);
    assert.equal(s.received.length, 0);
  } finally {
    await s.close();
  }
});

await check("SMTP: connection refused is a TransportError; URLs parse", async () => {
  const s = await fakeSmtp();
  const port = s.port;
  await s.close();
  await assert.rejects(smtpTransport({ host: "127.0.0.1", port }).send(msg()), (e: unknown) => e instanceof TransportError && /Cannot connect/.test(e.message));
  assert.deepEqual(parseSmtpUrl("smtps://u%40x.in:p%2Fw@smtp.example.com"), { host: "smtp.example.com", port: 465, secure: true, user: "u@x.in", pass: "p/w" });
  assert.deepEqual(parseSmtpUrl("smtp://smtp.example.com:2525"), { host: "smtp.example.com", port: 2525, secure: false });
  assert.throws(() => parseSmtpUrl("http://x"), /smtp:\/\//);
});

// ---- mailer ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

const resetData = MAIL_TEMPLATES["password-reset"].sample;

await check("mailer without a queue sends directly (standalone)", async () => {
  const transport = memoryTransport();
  const mailer = createMailer({ transport, from: "MGPL <no-reply@example.com>" });
  const out = await mailer.send("password-reset", resetData, { to: "kavita@example.com" });
  assert.equal(out.via, "direct");
  assert.equal(transport.sent.length, 1);
  assert.equal(transport.sent[0]!.subject, "Reset your password");
  assert.match(transport.sent[0]!.text, /sample-token/);
});

await check("mailer with an available queue enqueues; the worker processor delivers the job", async () => {
  const transport = memoryTransport();
  const added: { name: string; data: MailJob; opts?: Record<string, unknown> }[] = [];
  const fakeQueue = { add: async (name: string, data: MailJob, opts?: Record<string, unknown>) => (added.push({ name, data, opts }), { id: "42" }) };
  const mailer = createMailer({ transport, from: "no-reply@example.com", queue: queueAdapter(fakeQueue, { available: () => true }) });
  const out = await mailer.send("password-reset", resetData, { to: "kavita@example.com" });
  assert.deepEqual(out, { via: "queue", jobId: "42" });
  assert.equal(transport.sent.length, 0);
  assert.equal(added[0]!.name, "mail");
  assert.equal(added[0]!.opts!.removeOnComplete, true, "jobs holding reset links do not linger");
  // the job survives JSON (as in Redis) and the worker sends it
  const job = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(added[0]!.data)) as MailJob;
  const result = await mailProcessor(mailer)({ data: job });
  assert.deepEqual(result.accepted, ["kavita@example.com"]);
  assert.equal(transport.sent.length, 1);
});

await check("mailer falls back to direct when the queue is down or enqueue fails", async () => {
  const transport = memoryTransport();
  const reasons: unknown[] = [];
  const down = createMailer({ transport, from: "no-reply@example.com", queue: { enqueue: async () => "x", available: () => false }, onFallback: (r) => reasons.push(r) });
  assert.equal((await down.send("password-reset", resetData, { to: "a@example.com" })).via, "direct");
  const failing = createMailer({ transport, from: "no-reply@example.com", queue: { enqueue: () => Promise.reject(new Error("ECONNREFUSED")) }, onFallback: (r) => reasons.push(r) });
  assert.equal((await failing.send("password-reset", resetData, { to: "a@example.com" })).via, "direct");
  assert.equal(transport.sent.length, 2);
  assert.equal(reasons.length, 2);
  const strict = createMailer({ transport, from: "no-reply@example.com", queue: { enqueue: () => Promise.reject(new Error("down")) }, whenQueueFails: "throw" });
  await assert.rejects(strict.send("password-reset", resetData, { to: "a@example.com" }), (e: unknown) => e instanceof MailError && e.code === "MAIL_QUEUE");
});

await check("mailer validates before queueing: unknown template, missing data, bad address", async () => {
  const added: unknown[] = [];
  const mailer = createMailer({ transport: memoryTransport(), from: "no-reply@example.com", queue: { enqueue: async (j) => (added.push(j), "1") } });
  await assert.rejects(mailer.send("nope", {}, { to: "a@example.com" }), (e: unknown) => e instanceof MailError && e.code === "MAIL_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE");
  await assert.rejects(mailer.send("toString", {}, { to: "a@example.com" }), /Unknown mail template/);
  await assert.rejects(mailer.send("password-reset", { name: "x" }, { to: "a@example.com" }), MissingVariableError);
  await assert.rejects(mailer.send("password-reset", resetData, { to: "not an address" }), /Not an email address/);
  await assert.rejects(mailer.send("password-reset", resetData, { to: [] }), /at least one recipient/);
  assert.equal(added.length, 0);
  assert.throws(() => createMailer({ transport: memoryTransport(), from: "bad" }), /Not an email address/);
});

await check("mailer: custom templates, brand, reply-to and per-mail sender", async () => {
  const transport = memoryTransport();
  const hello = defineMail({ id: "hello", description: "", source: mail("Hello {{ who }}", "subject: Hi {{ who }}"), sample: { who: "Lab" } });
  const mailer = createMailer({ transport, from: "a@example.com", replyTo: "desk@example.com", templates: { ...MAIL_TEMPLATES, hello }, brand: { name: "Branch Lab" } });
  await mailer.send("hello", { who: "Asha" }, { to: "b@example.com", from: "Branch <branch@example.com>" });
  const m = transport.sent[0]!;
  assert.equal(m.subject, "Hi Asha");
  assert.equal(m.from, "Branch <branch@example.com>");
  assert.equal(m.replyTo, "desk@example.com");
  assert.match(m.text, /Branch Lab/);
  assert.ok(mailer.templates().includes("hello") && mailer.templates().includes("password-reset"));
});

// ---- report ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

if (failures.length) {
  console.error(failures.join("\n"));
  console.error(`\n${failures.length} failed, ${passed} passed`);
  process.exit(1);
}
console.log(`mail-kit: ${passed} checks passed`);
```

## File: src/define.ts

```ts
import { parseMail } from "./parse";
import { mailVariables, renderMail, type RenderOptions } from "./render";
import type { MailDocument, RenderedMail } from "./types";

export interface MailTemplate<D extends Record<string, unknown> = Record<string, unknown>> {
  id: string;
  description: string;
  /** The `.mail` source. */
  source: string;
  document: MailDocument;
  /** Every variable path the template reads. */
  variables: string[];
  /** Fictional data that renders the template completely (previews and tests). */
  sample: D;
  render(data: D, opts?: RenderOptions): RenderedMail;
}

/** A template of any data shape (for registries such as MAIL_TEMPLATES). */
// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
export type AnyMailTemplate = MailTemplate<any>;

/**
 * Declares a mail. The source is parsed here, so a syntax error fails at startup (and in tests),
 * never while sending.
 */
export function defineMail<D extends Record<string, unknown>>(def: { id: string; description: string; source: string; sample: D }): MailTemplate<D> {
  const document = parseMail(def.source, def.id);
  return {
    ...def,
    document,
    variables: mailVariables(document),
    render: (data, opts) => renderMail(document, data, opts),
  };
}
```

## File: src/errors.ts

```ts
import type { Pos } from "./types";

/** Error codes are a public contract: add new ones, never rename. */
export type MailErrorCode =
  | "MAIL_SYNTAX"
  | "MAIL_MISSING_VARIABLE"
  | "MAIL_BAD_VALUE"
  | "MAIL_UNSAFE_URL"
  | "MAIL_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE"
  | "MAIL_BAD_ADDRESS"
  | "MAIL_TRANSPORT"
  | "MAIL_QUEUE";

export class MailError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly code: MailErrorCode,
    message: string,
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "MailError";
  }
}

export interface Diagnostic {
  message: string;
  line: number;
  col: number;
}

/** A `.mail` source that does not parse. Lists every problem with its line and column. */
export class MailSyntaxError extends MailError {
  constructor(
    readonly diagnostics: Diagnostic[],
    readonly file?: string,
  ) {
    super("MAIL_SYNTAX", diagnostics.map((d) => `${file ?? "mail"}:${d.line}:${d.col} ${d.message}`).join("\n"));
    this.name = "MailSyntaxError";
  }
}

/** Data passed to a template is missing values it uses. `paths` lists each one once. */
export class MissingVariableError extends MailError {
  constructor(readonly paths: string[]) {
    super("MAIL_MISSING_VARIABLE", `Missing mail variable${paths.length > 1 ? "s" : ""}: ${paths.join(", ")}`);
    this.name = "MissingVariableError";
  }
}

/** SMTP or provider failure. `status` is the SMTP reply code when there is one. */
export class TransportError extends MailError {
  constructor(
    message: string,
    readonly status?: number,
  ) {
    super("MAIL_TRANSPORT", message);
    this.name = "TransportError";
  }
}

export const at = (pos: Pos, message: string): Diagnostic => ({ message, line: pos.line, col: pos.col });
```

## File: src/mailer.ts

```ts
// The mailer: renders a template and sends it through the worker's queue when one is available,
// otherwise (no queue, queue unavailable, or enqueue failed) straight through the transport.
import type { AnyMailTemplate } from "./define";
import { MailError } from "./errors";
import { addressList, parseAddress } from "./mime";
import type { RenderOptions } from "./render";
import { MAIL_TEMPLATES } from "./templates";
import type { Address, Brand, Envelope, RenderedMail, SendResult, Theme, Transport } from "./types";

/**
 * What goes on the queue: the template id, its data and the envelope, never rendered HTML.
 * Data crosses JSON, so Dates arrive as ISO strings (the date filters accept both).
 */
export interface MailJob {
  v: 1;
  template: string;
  data: Record<string, unknown>;
  envelope: Envelope;
}

/** The worker's queue, seen from the mailer. Structural, so mail-kit needs no queue library. */
export interface MailQueue {
  /** Adds the job; resolves with its id. Rejecting makes the mailer send directly instead. */
  enqueue(job: MailJob): Promise<string | undefined>;
  /** Cheap check before enqueueing (e.g. the Redis connection is "ready"). Default: assume yes. */
  available?(): boolean | Promise<boolean>;
}

export type SendOutcome = { via: "queue"; jobId: string | undefined } | ({ via: "direct" } & SendResult);

export interface MailerOptions {
  transport: Transport;
  /** Default sender, e.g. `"Maa Gayatri Path Lab <no-reply@example.com>"`. */
  from: Address;
  replyTo?: Address;
  /** The worker's queue. Leave it out to always send directly (standalone). */
  queue?: MailQueue;
  /**
   * When the queue is set but unavailable or enqueueing fails: "direct" (default) sends straight
   * away; "throw" raises MailError MAIL_QUEUE so the caller decides.
   */
  whenQueueFails?: "direct" | "throw";
  /** Called whenever a queued send fell back to sending directly (log it). */
  onFallback?: (reason: unknown, job: MailJob) => void;
  /** Templates by id. Default: the built-in MAIL_TEMPLATES; spread them to add your own. */
  templates?: Record<string, AnyMailTemplate>;
  brand?: Brand;
  theme?: Theme;
}

export interface Mailer {
  /**
   * Renders `template` with `data` (so bad data fails here, in the request, not in the worker)
   * and queues it, or sends it directly when there is no usable queue.
   */
  send(template: string, data: Record<string, unknown>, envelope: Envelope): Promise<SendOutcome>;
  /** Renders and sends now, ignoring the queue. The worker calls this for each job. */
  deliver(job: MailJob): Promise<SendResult>;
  /** Renders without sending (previews). */
  render(template: string, data: Record<string, unknown>): RenderedMail;
  /** The template ids this mailer knows. */
  templates(): string[];
  close(): Promise<void>;
}

export function createMailer(o: MailerOptions): Mailer {
  const templates: Record<string, AnyMailTemplate> = o.templates ?? MAIL_TEMPLATES;
  const renderOpts: RenderOptions = { ...(o.brand ? { brand: o.brand } : {}), ...(o.theme ? { theme: o.theme } : {}) };
  parseAddress(o.from);

  const get = (id: string): AnyMailTemplate => {
    const t = Object.hasOwn(templates, id) ? templates[id] : undefined;
    if (!t) throw new MailError("MAIL_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE", `Unknown mail template "${id}" (known: ${Object.keys(templates).join(", ")})`);
    return t;
  };
  const render = (id: string, data: Record<string, unknown>) => get(id).render(data, renderOpts);
  const checkEnvelope = (e: Envelope) => {
    const n = addressList(e.to).length + addressList(e.cc).length + addressList(e.bcc).length;
    if (!n) throw new MailError("MAIL_BAD_ADDRESS", "A mail needs at least one recipient");
    if (e.replyTo) parseAddress(e.replyTo);
    if (e.from) parseAddress(e.from);
  };

  const deliver = async (job: MailJob): Promise<SendResult> => {
    if (job.v !== 1) throw new MailError("MAIL_QUEUE", `Unsupported mail job version ${String(job.v)}`);
    const mail = render(job.template, job.data);
    const replyTo = job.envelope.replyTo ?? o.replyTo;
    return o.transport.send({
      ...job.envelope,
      from: job.envelope.from ?? o.from,
      ...(replyTo ? { replyTo } : {}),
      subject: mail.subject,
      html: mail.html,
      text: mail.text,
    });
  };

  return {
    async send(template, data, envelope) {
      render(template, data);
      checkEnvelope(envelope);
      const job: MailJob = { v: 1, template, data, envelope };
      if (o.queue) {
        let reason: unknown;
        try {
          if ((await (o.queue.available?.() ?? true)) === true) {
            return { via: "queue", jobId: await o.queue.enqueue(job) };
          }
          reason = new MailError("MAIL_QUEUE", "Mail queue is not available");
        } catch (e) {
          reason = e;
        }
        if (o.whenQueueFails === "throw") {
          throw reason instanceof MailError ? reason : new MailError("MAIL_QUEUE", `Could not queue the mail: ${reason instanceof Error ? reason.message : String(reason)}`);
        }
        o.onFallback?.(reason, job);
      }
      return { via: "direct", ...(await deliver(job)) };
    },
    deliver,
    render,
    templates: () => Object.keys(templates),
    close: async () => {
      await o.transport.close?.();
    },
  };
}
```

## File: src/mime.ts

```ts
// RFC 5322 / MIME message builder: multipart/alternative (text + HTML), quoted-printable UTF-8,
// RFC 2047 encoded headers. Header values are checked for CR/LF so nothing can inject headers.
import { randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
import { MailError } from "./errors";
import type { Address, OutgoingMessage } from "./types";

const EMAIL = /^[^\s@<>()",;:\\[\]]+@[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?)+$/;

export interface ParsedAddress {
  name?: string;
  email: string;
}

/** Accepts "a@b.in", "Name <a@b.in>" or { name, email }. Throws MAIL_BAD_ADDRESS otherwise. */
export function parseAddress(a: Address): ParsedAddress {
  let name: string | undefined;
  let email: string;
  if (typeof a === "string") {
    const m = /^\s*(?:"?([^"<]*?)"?\s*)?<([^<>]+)>\s*$/.exec(a);
    if (m) {
      name = m[1]?.trim() || undefined;
      email = m[2]!.trim();
    } else email = a.trim();
  } else {
    name = a.name?.trim() || undefined;
    email = a.email.trim();
  }
  if (!EMAIL.test(email) || email.length > 254) throw new MailError("MAIL_BAD_ADDRESS", `Not an email address: "${email}"`);
  if (name && /[\r\n]/.test(name)) throw new MailError("MAIL_BAD_ADDRESS", "Address names cannot contain line breaks");
  return name ? { name, email } : { email };
}

export const addressList = (a: Address | Address[] | undefined): ParsedAddress[] => (a === undefined ? [] : (Array.isArray(a) ? a : [a]).map(parseAddress));

const ascii = (s: string) => /^[\x20-\x7e]*$/.test(s);

/** RFC 2047 "B" encoded-words, split so each stays under 75 characters and never cuts a character. */
export function encodeWord(s: string): string {
  if (ascii(s)) return s;
  const words: string[] = [];
  let cur = "";
  for (const ch of s) {
    if (Buffer.byteLength(cur + ch) > 45) {
      words.push(cur);
      cur = "";
    }
    cur += ch;
  }
  if (cur) words.push(cur);
  return words.map((w) => `=?UTF-8?B?${Buffer.from(w).toString("base64")}?=`).join("\r\n ");
}

export function formatAddress(a: ParsedAddress): string {
  if (!a.name) return a.email;
  const name = ascii(a.name) ? (/^[A-Za-z0-9!#$%&'*+\-/=?^_`{|}~ ]+$/.test(a.name) ? a.name : `"${a.name.replace(/(["\\])/g, "\\$1")}"`) : encodeWord(a.name);
  return `${name} <${a.email}>`;
}

/** Quoted-printable (RFC 2045) with CRLF line ends and soft breaks at 76 characters. */
export function quotedPrintable(input: string): string {
  const lines = input.replace(/\r\n?/g, "\n").split("\n");
  return lines
    .map((line) => {
      let out = "";
      let len = 0;
      const bytes = Buffer.from(line, "utf8");
      for (let k = 0; k < bytes.length; k++) {
        const b = bytes[k]!;
        const last = k === bytes.length - 1;
        let enc: string;
        if ((b >= 33 && b <= 126 && b !== 61) || ((b === 32 || b === 9) && !last)) enc = String.fromCharCode(b);
        else enc = "=" + b.toString(16).toUpperCase().padStart(2, "0");
        if (len + enc.length > 75) {
          out += "=\r\n";
          len = 0;
        }
        out += enc;
        len += enc.length;
      }
      return out;
    })
    .join("\r\n");
}

function checkHeader(name: string, value: string): void {
  if (/[\r\n]/.test(value) || !/^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$/.test(name)) throw new MailError("MAIL_BAD_VALUE", `Header ${name} cannot contain line breaks`);
}

export interface BuiltMessage {
  /** The whole message, CRLF line ends, ready for SMTP DATA (before dot-stuffing). */
  raw: string;
  messageId: string;
  from: string;
  /** Every envelope recipient (to + cc + bcc), deduplicated. */
  recipients: string[];
}

/** Builds the MIME message for `msg`. `domain` is used for the Message-ID. */
export function buildMessage(msg: OutgoingMessage, opts: { date?: Date } = {}): BuiltMessage {
  const from = parseAddress(msg.from);
  const to = addressList(msg.to);
  const cc = addressList(msg.cc);
  const bcc = addressList(msg.bcc);
  if (!to.length && !cc.length && !bcc.length) throw new MailError("MAIL_BAD_ADDRESS", "A message needs at least one recipient");
  const replyTo = msg.replyTo ? parseAddress(msg.replyTo) : null;
  checkHeader("Subject", msg.subject);
  const domain = from.email.split("@")[1]!;
  const messageId = `<${Date.now().toString(36)}.${randomBytes(9).toString("hex")}@${domain}>`;
  const boundary = `mk_${randomBytes(12).toString("hex")}`;

  const headers: [string, string][] = [
    ["From", formatAddress(from)],
    ...(to.length ? ([["To", to.map(formatAddress).join(",\r\n ")]] as [string, string][]) : []),
    ...(cc.length ? ([["Cc", cc.map(formatAddress).join(",\r\n ")]] as [string, string][]) : []),
    ...(replyTo ? ([["Reply-To", formatAddress(replyTo)]] as [string, string][]) : []),
    ["Subject", encodeWord(msg.subject)],
    ["Date", (opts.date ?? new Date()).toUTCString().replace("GMT", "+0000")],
    ["Message-ID", messageId],
    ["MIME-Version", "1.0"],
  ];
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(msg.headers ?? {})) {
    checkHeader(k, v);
    if (/^(from|to|cc|bcc|subject|date|message-id|mime-version|content-type|content-transfer-encoding|reply-to)$/i.test(k)) {
      throw new MailError("MAIL_BAD_VALUE", `Header ${k} is set by mail-kit`);
    }
    headers.push([k, encodeWord(v)]);
  }
  headers.push(["Content-Type", `multipart/alternative; boundary="${boundary}"`]);

  const part = (type: string, body: string) =>
    [`--${boundary}`, `Content-Type: ${type}; charset=utf-8`, "Content-Transfer-Encoding: quoted-printable", "", quotedPrintable(body)].join("\r\n");
  const raw = [headers.map(([k, v]) => `${k}: ${v}`).join("\r\n"), "", part("text/plain", msg.text), part("text/html", msg.html), `--${boundary}--`, ""].join("\r\n");
  const recipients = [...new Set([...to, ...cc, ...bcc].map((a) => a.email))];
  return { raw, messageId, from: from.email, recipients };
}
```
